items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: if Miles Davis’ group was taking a flight to Paris, it costs the same for my group to go to Paris.

ctx.x: Well he just doesn’t know. I don’t know why or even how or why he would even make such a statement because he obviously hasn’t been or doesn’t see the things that I see, and see what a lot of other — it’s a different time than when the music that even like what you presented with Joe Williams — that’s a different era. It was a different place. And even before that, that music was really popular. I mean the pop music of that day. We’ve lost that. I mean even Broadway, because a lot of those songs came through…

they weren’t all that — I mean nobody got rich off those clubs. They got a lot of notoriety that they could play, and you learned how to play. One of the things we’re missing is a network of going from state to state, city to city, to keep the music vibrant. The airlines, the economic — whatever you want to — has made it difficult. It still costs, if Miles Davis’ group was taking a flight to Paris, it costs the same for my group to go to Paris. And he’s making ten or twenty thousand times more money than I’m…
You had to love it, right?
